update_engine: Parse and supply EOL date for Chrome From Omaha, the optional field |_eol_date| is to indicate the EOL of a device. Chrome side will leverage these values to display a notification. The value for |_eol_date| should be an integer value indicating the days from Unix Epoch date. If |_eol_date| does not exist in the Omaha response or have non-integer values, the default will fallback to |kEolDateInvalid|. pd_faft: Perform PDTester initiated items first, for safety reason In firmware_PDVbusRequest test, it performs: * DUT initiated items, which PDTester is fixed to 20V and DUT initates the requests of 5V, 12V, or 20V (or the max input voltage DUT supports). * PDTester initiated items, which PDTester changes to support max 5V, 12V, or 20V, and DUT reacts to request the max voltage. The DUT initiated items is more risky. If the DUT max input voltage is not 20V, like 12V, and the FAFT config is set wrong, it may negotiate to to a voltage higher than it can support, that may damage the DUT. The PDTester initiated items is safe. If the DUT max input voltage is not 20V, it tries to negotiate the best. So it should not damage the DUT. If it does damage DUT, this is also what we want to discover. This CL swaps the order and performs the PDTester initiated items first. If any item fails, possibly the FAFT config not set properly, it stops the test and doesn't perform the risky DUT initiated items. BUG=b:139372561 TEST=Ran firmware_PDVbusRequest. Made the PDTester initiated items failed and checked it not perform the DUT initiated items. Change-Id: I971c0383ca11754604a0ae57f6b074e7913809b2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1823930 Tested-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Commit-Ready: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dana Goyette <dgoyette@chromium.org>

tpm_manager: remove stale local data from the disk After TPM ownership is cleared, tpm manager local data becomes stale. If it's somehow not wiped after reboot/encstateful remount, the stale data will show up in TPM status (e.g., the output of `tpm_manager_client status`) and/or be reused by tpm manager again. This change detects and removes stale local data shortly after tpm_managerd starts. BUG=chromium:974313 TEST=Unit tests. On a soraka: 1. Take tpm ownership, define a new NV space, soft-clear tpm, restart tpm_managerd, run tpm_manager_client status, and make sure all the stale data is gone, including the nvram policy. 2. Following 1, define another new NV space, restart tpm_managerd, run tpm_manager_client status again, and make sure a policy of the new space is added. 3. Following 2, take ownership, restart tpm_managerd, and make sure the new local data isn't removed. 4. Manually modify trunks utility to fail after the endorsement password is set, soft-clear tpm, restart tpm_managerd, and take ownership. Make sure take ownership fails but local data contains the new passwords. Then, restart tpm_managerd and make sure nothing is wiped in the local data. On a chell: Do the same tests above by replacing soft-clearing tpm with backing up and restoring stale /var/lib/tpm_manager/local_tpm_data, simulating an unwiped encstateful. Change-Id: I351a82f1843f6e752c7b46433c80c2def4b14535 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1765808 Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com>

bluetooth: Add debug info on first failure of test functions Our test functionality is run with a _test_retry_and_log decorator that re-tries a function in case of failure. After the second failure, the test is marked as failed and the return value of the function is printed. However, the return value of the first run is equally, if not more important for debugging the cause of failure, so this patch prints out the return value of the first failure. BUG=None TEST=cause failures in autotest and observe Change-Id: Id738d24f77366247b77d21b44ce71009b62df5ef Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1814223 Tested-by: Daniel Winkler <danielwinkler@google.com> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yun-Hao Chung <howardchung@google.com>

bluetooth: Use dbus::ObjectPath type instead of string The properties "Device" and "Service" need to use dbus::ObjectPath type to be BlueZ-compliant. This requires changing *ToObjectPath converters to return dbus::ObjectPath type. Otherwise, wrongly using string type for "Device" and "Service" properties may cause clients to not recognize these properties.
